subject: the two SKILL.md files are reachable from Claude Code only; pi never reads .claude/skills/
activeForm: Making the repo's skills reachable from both harnesses

work_items: Make canon-audit and adversarial-repo-mapping reachable from pi as well as Claude Code, as one copy each
Verify each is actually listed by the harness that is supposed to load it, rather than inferring it from the directory shape

description:
REPORTED by scottgoscott's Helios through the board inbox 2026-09-22 and verified here against the installed pi before carding.

THE FACT. This repo carries .claude/skills/canon-audit/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/adversarial-repo-mapping/SKILL.md. pi never reads .claude/skills/: `grep -rno '\.claude[/\\]skills' <pi>/dist/` returns zero hits across the whole distribution. pi's project resource roots are <cwd>/.pi/{extensions,skills,prompts,themes} (package-manager.js:1962-1967), plus ~/.agents/skills, neither of which exists here. So both skills are loaded by Claude Code alone, and every pi session in this repo -- which includes every Dynamo, since card-start launches pi -- has them available nowhere.

CORRECTION TO THE REPORT'S PROPOSED FIX. It recommends moving them to .pi/prompts/<name>.md. That is right for workflow commands and wrong for these two. pi loads SKILL.md natively: skills.js:117-137 treats any directory containing a SKILL.md as a skill root and recurses to find them. The pi-native home is therefore .pi/skills/<name>/SKILL.md -- the same directory shape and the same filename these already have, with the same name/description frontmatter. Moving them to prompts/ instead would convert model-invoked skills into slash commands and drop their auto-invocation, which is a behaviour change rather than a relocation.

THE OPEN QUESTION, which is why this is a card and not a commit. 'One copy each' needs a home chosen, and both harnesses are live in this repo: Dynamos are pi, the operator's own sessions have been Claude Code. Options are a single .pi/skills/ copy with .claude/skills/ symlinked at it (untested here -- confirm Claude Code follows the symlink before relying on it), a single copy in whichever harness actually uses them, or accepting dual maintenance with a note. Dual maintenance is what silently diverges, which is the reason the report was sent.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than the two files: the reporting repo had five workflow prompts as flat .claude/skills/<name>.md files, which is NEITHER harness's format, so five commands documented as available in its CLAUDE.md had never existed in either harness. Verify a skill or prompt is listed by the harness that should load it; a plausible directory shape is not evidence.
